criteria.cgo_official: Adopt pg_query_go/v6 v6.2.2: the official tagged release, cold runs near 5 ms, batch RSS near 12 MB, and a 13461954-byte test binary. canlc builds then need clang with CGO_ENABLED=1, replacing the present CGO_ENABLED=0 launcher compilation; the plan already treats that toolchain as a builder-only prerequisite rather than a user runtime need.
criteria.review_needed: The supplied measurements cannot separate the bindings, or neither one satisfies the stated contracts.
criteria.wasm_wazero: Adopt go-pgquery v0.0.0-20260915022521-81f99195012b on wazero v1.12.0: builds stay pure Go with zero C dependencies and equivalent parser/scanner results, while each SQL-bearing run pays a single ~454 ms just-in-time compile with a ~300 MB short-lived peak, carries a 20639362-byte binary, and tracks an untagged outside revision.

binding_choice.instructions: Pick which SQL parser binding becomes the pinned production dependency, the official CGo one or the WASM/wazero one. Consult common together with topics.binding_choice.

criteria.closed_reasons: Translate every failure into a tiny closed catalogue of reasons (syntax, scanner, empty, and multi-statement shapes, for instance) attached to the cursor position, relegating the upstream sentence to supporting detail. No matcher reads upstream wording; unseen failure shapes join the catalogue through deliberate extension.
criteria.review_needed: The supplied evidence cannot settle the failure vocabulary, or neither vocabulary satisfies the stated contracts.
criteria.verbatim_upstream: Pass the upstream sentence and character cursor through untouched, projecting the cursor onto byte ranges of the manifest statement. Reports cite PostgreSQL language directly; I37 sorts outcomes by which spans exist instead of by message content, accepting that phrasing can drift between parser releases.

error_vocabulary.instructions: Decide if adapter failures keep the upstream message plus cursor word for word or collapse into a closed reason catalogue that demotes the message. Consult common together with topics.error_vocabulary.

criteria.bundled_call: Offer a single per-descriptor adapter routine that executes upstream Parse and Scan back to back and hands back one compiler-owned record with statements, tokens, spans, and any failure. No caller ever sees a parse result divorced from its token stream.
criteria.review_needed: The supplied evidence cannot settle the call shape, or neither shape satisfies the stated contracts.
criteria.separate_calls: Offer Parse and Scan as two standalone adapter routines with their own compiler-owned result shapes. I37 calls each exactly once per descriptor, and either pass can be exercised or reused on its own.

result_packaging.instructions: Decide between a single adapter routine that bundles parse plus scan and two independent Parse/Scan routines. Consult common together with topics.result_packaging.

fixed_constraints: P12 commits to libpg_query on a single PostgreSQL major and demands the genuine parser and scanner: a lone approved statement in each descriptor, dense $1..$N application parameters, scanner byte ranges that carve static SQL into Bun tagged-template pieces, and a top-level LIMIT carried by its own trailing parameter. Hand-rolled SQL lexers, parsers, and query machinery are forbidden, backend-flavoured ASTs must not leak across checker files, and a scanner gap never justifies a fallback lexer.

The two evaluated contenders both wrap PostgreSQL 17.7 (PG_VERSION_NUM 170007): pg_query_go/v6 v6.2.2 from 2026-01-28 bundling libpg_query 17-6.2.2, and go-pgquery v0.0.0-20260915022521-81f99195012b from 2026-09-15 bundling wazero v1.12.0 with a 2488452-byte embedded WebAssembly module translated from identical 17.7 sources. go-pgquery emits pg_query_go/v6 protobuf types.

A 24-example suite (plain/repeated/multi-digit parameters, single-quoted/escape/dollar-quoted strings, line plus nested block comments, multibyte UTF-8 ahead of tokens, broken grammar, unterminated strings, multi/empty/comment-only/semicolon-only inputs, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE with and without RETURNING, subquery and literal LIMIT) shows byte-equal raw parse and scan JSON, token ranges, statement ranges, parameter numbers and ranges, and failure message with cursor. The lone divergence is the Go error wrapper label (*parser.Error against *pgerror.Error).

Apple M4 darwin/arm64 figures: a fresh process parsing plus scanning the 105-byte P13 SELECT needs roughly 5 ms wall (1 ms in-library) through CGo against roughly 454 ms wall (447 ms in-library, single wazero compilation) through WASM. Steady state: parse near 14 us with 3.3 KB across 70 allocations (CGo) against near 45 us with 85 KB across 78 allocations (WASM); scan near 2 us against 5 us. Test binaries: CGo 13461954 bytes; WASM 20639362 bytes, shrinking to 15403074 bytes under CGO_ENABLED=0. Clean-cache builds last 6.7 s (CGo, clang required) against 7.4 s (WASM, Go alone). A 1200 parse+scan batch crests around 12 MB RSS (CGo) against around 300 MB fleeting RSS (WASM, 12 MB kept under GC pressure).

Distribution realities: distribution/build.go currently builds the launcher under CGO_ENABLED=0; plan.md accepts Go/C build tooling for source builds tied to the SQL binding pick while shipped users need none. CGo is pganalyze's official line with tagged cuts (BSD-3-Clause plus PostgreSQL License); WASM is an external line without tags (pseudo-version pin), MIT plus BSD NOTICE plus PostgreSQL-derived bytes plus Apache-2.0 wazero, requiring WebAssembly threads and exception handling as shipped by wazero 1.12.0. canlc checks every SQL descriptor inside brief batch runs.
common.purpose: Guide the Can compiler using only the material handed over in this request. No web lookups, no coding, no prose answers. If the material leaves contenders indistinguishable, take the flagged uncertainty option.

binding_choice.facts: canlc examines each SQL manifest descriptor a single time per check inside a short batch run, with project descriptor totals in the tens. CGo holds each canlc run quick and small yet demands clang and CGO_ENABLED=1 on every machine that builds canlc, overturning today's CGO_ENABLED=0 launcher build. WASM holds canlc builds free of C yet bills each SQL-bearing run a one-off ~450 ms compilation with a ~300 MB fleeting crest, enlarges the binary, and freezes an untagged external commit. Parser trees, scanner tokens, byte ranges, and failure message/cursor pairs coincide exactly.

error_vocabulary.facts: Both contenders describe a failure with a message plus Cursorpos, a character displacement in the statement, next to source routine, file, line, and possible extra context. Can manifest diagnostics want byte ranges over can.project.json statement bytes plus a durable category that I37 can branch on without scraping upstream sentences. Upstream sentences evolve between libpg_query cuts; cursor displacements hold steady for fixed input on a fixed parser.

result_packaging.facts: libpg_query publishes parsing and scanning through distinct entry points; one descriptor wants the statement roster with ranges out of Parse and the token flow with ranges out of Scan. A combined adapter routine hides both behind one Go signature returning a single record; split routines expose each pass on its own for I37 to call. Descriptor validation runs a single time per compile, with zero runtime re-parsing.
